A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniDrive with matching authors, core methods and experiments. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v2 adds a readable visualization appendix.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.4, Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–5 report original CARLA 3D detection experiments across camera configurations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CARLA detection experiments in Tables 1–2 and Figures 5–6, and adds virtual-camera projection examples in Appendix A.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 revises the specified projection computation: Equation (1) adds horizontal focal-length normalization, and Equation (2) uses separately normalized horizontal and vertical coordinates. This is a localized computational correction; the virtual-camera pipeline, blending and CMA-ES optimization remain unchanged. Implementation changes are not documented.

E1.justification: Both evaluate six-class 3D detection using CARLA Towns 1–6 and the same camera-configuration scenarios. Appendix A visualizes four existing configurations without introducing a new dataset, task or domain.

E2.justification: BEVFusion-C remains the sole external evaluated baseline. Both versions retain the comparison between optimized and unoptimized UniDrive. The added related-work citation does not introduce an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both retain 500 scenes and 20,000 frames per configuration, a 250/250 training-validation scene split, 1600×900 images, AP/mAP reporting and the same cross-configuration testing design. The added visualizations do not specify a different evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Appendix A and Figure 7 add a qualitative examination of projected images across four existing camera configurations, exposing regions left unwarped. The optimization comparison and camera-intrinsic, height and placement ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Reporting remains based on point estimates.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and the detection and ablation plots match across versions after figure renumbering. Appendix A adds qualitative projection outputs and reports generally accurate warping with some uncovered regions; no revised detection performance is reported.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(2) receive substantive geometric corrections: the ground-plane horizontal coordinate gains a factor of 1/fx, and the fixed-distance ray formulation accommodates unequal horizontal and vertical focal lengths. The projection-error objective and CMA-ES derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the claims of cross-configuration perception through ground-aware virtual views, projection-error optimization, plug-and-play integration and a 160,000-frame CARLA benchmark. Their scientific scope and central novelty claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly attributes unwarped regions to missing coverage from the original cameras, qualifying its assessment of projection accuracy. The existing interpretations of robustness and limitations concerning simulation-only evaluation and the restricted range of tested configurations remain.

D1.justification: v2 removes the abstract's explicit code-and-benchmark repository link while retaining the project-homepage link. This reduces direct access information without establishing that resources were withdrawn. No new training hyperparameters, hardware or runtime details are supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds Li et al. (2024b), 'Is your lidar placement optimized for 3d scene understanding?', to the sensor-configuration discussion and references. It also softens BEVFusion's description from a leading state-of-the-art approach to a representative method; the broader positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized wording and grammar edits, configuration-notation and cross-reference adjustments, an ICLR 2025 publication header, and a short visualization appendix. The main section order and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds an integration diagram as Figure 3, two virtual-configuration panels to the former Figure 3, now Figure 4, and projection examples as Figure 7. Existing result plots are renumbered, and table spacing and page flow are adjusted without a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the documented projection geometry through the corrections in Equations (1)–(2), while the integration diagram and Appendix A make the method and its coverage limitation easier to inspect. Experimental scope and numerical evidence remain unchanged. Removing the direct repository link weakens access documentation, but the retained project link and gains in correctness and explanation support a limited net improvement.
